headline: Authum Investment & Infrastructure to subscribe to subsidiary ISARC shares via rights issue
sum: Authum Investment & Infrastructure Limited announced a subscription to shares of its subsidiary ISARC through a rights issue, signalling capital infusion into the subsidiary for working capital or growth purposes.
implication: Rights issues to parent companies by subsidiaries create complexities under Companies Act 2013 (preferential allotment rules) and require careful structuring of board approval, valuation, and disclosure to avoid breach of prohibitions on financial assistance; structure establishes precedent for intra-group capital transfers via equity.
detail: Authum Investment & Infrastructure Limited, a Delhi-registered holding/infrastructure company, announced subscription to newly issued shares of its subsidiary ISARC (likely Infrastructure Services & Resources Company or similar) through a rights issue mechanism. The subsidiary offered shares via rights to existing shareholders (in this case, the parent), enabling direct equity participation without open market issuance. Such transactions are common for funded growth in subsidiaries but require board resolutions, preferential allotment compliance under the Companies Act 2013, and RoC notification. No acquisition price, share count, or final draw date has been publicly disclosed in the available source.

framework.note: Preferential allotment of shares by subsidiary to parent; requires board approval, shareholder consent (if applicable), and valuation by independent merchant banker.
Prohibition on financial assistance for purchase of shares; rights issues by subsidiaries to parents must not breach this unless carved out by statute.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, reg. 5 & 6
framework.note: If subsidiary is listed, preferential issue must comply with listing rules and SEBI-ICDR; disclosure of valuation and board minutes mandatory.

framework.ref: Listing Agreement / National Stock Exchange Rules (if ISARC is listed)
framework.note: Related-party transaction disclosure and regulation of intra-group share transfers.
Subscription at less than fair market value may attract income tax on the subsidiary for the difference; valuation certificate critical.
Form MGT-14 (Board resolution), Form PAS-2 (share allotment), and annual filing must disclose subsidiary capital structure and rights issue mechanics.

framework.ref: Reserve Bank of India – Consolidated FDI Policy (if applicable to foreign shareholders)
framework.note: If either entity has foreign investment, intra-group equity transfers may trigger FDI compliance.

conditions: Board approval by subsidiary (ISARC) for rights issue
Parent company subscription agreement and payment of subscription amount
Compliance with preferential allotment rules under Companies Act 2013, s. 62
Independent merchant banker valuation (if subsidiary is listed or consideration >₹100 cr)
RoC filing of board resolution and allotment notice
approvals: NSE/BSE notification (if either entity is listed)
structure.novel: Use of rights issue mechanism for intra-group capital transfer; indicates potential subsidiary recapitalisation or dividend reinvestment.

triggers.note: Preferential allotment rules apply; subsidiary must follow statutory procedure.

triggers.law: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations 2015 (if applicable)
triggers.note: Related-party transaction disclosure required if either party is listed.
Mandatory notification of share allotment within 30 days.
